answer: A spiral reputation ladder resists Sybil attacks by making each identity climb slowly: newcomers start in a shared nebula of unverified agents and earn trust only through small, randomly assigned verification tasks checked by independent peers. Each verified task cracks open one layer of a walnut-hard bond — a refundable stake that grows with proven work — so creating many fake identities costs far more in locked stake and waiting time than any single identity can gain.
